reasons.demand: PROVISIONAL, pending replies: 0 of 19 outreach drafts sent yet (Nick decided 2026-10-24 to keep the free NHTSA exposure sheet, so the pitch is final). Pain is real (state AGs have forced CarMax and 100+ NY dealers to disclose open recalls; a federal used-car recall bill was reintroduced Sept 2025) but Michigan has no disclosure law, and NHTSA already gives dealers a free 100-VIN batch lookup, so urgency for a small independent lot is unproven. Raise to 3-4 if 3+ of 19 reply yes/maybe.
reasons.repeat_use: PROVISIONAL, pending replies: Subscription-shaped: inventory turns every few weeks and NHTSA posts new campaigns daily, so a weekly sheet stays useful. Capped at 4 because the free NHTSA tool covers the same need for a patient dealer.
reasons.competition: PROVISIONAL, pending replies: Crowded and the incumbents have the better data. Carfax gives its dealer subscribers recall monitoring on inventory; AutoCheck sells an Open Recall Inventory Check; Recall Masters and AutoAp sell daily VIN-level recall management (true open/closed status, which free NHTSA data cannot give); NHTSA's own site checks 100 VINs at a time for free. Nick's positioning (2026-10-24): we are not buying VIN-level data; the product is free-data, simpler and cheaper than Carfax/AutoAp, and can be offered free if that is what wins the first lots. That is an edge on price and simplicity, not on data, so the score stays 2.
reasons.license: NHTSA vPIC, Recalls API and ODI flat files are US Government works (public domain), no key, no terms restricting commercial use found on nhtsa.gov. Verified at G0 with live requests. No paid data deal, so no third-party license enters the product.
reasons.build_effort: PROVISIONAL, pending replies: Nick fixed the product on 2026-10-24 as the smaller exposure sheet that refresh.py already produces from core (CSV/HTML/landscape PDF). Remaining work is inventory intake (CSV/email), flat-file ingest to dodge the API 400s, per-dealer scheduling and delivery: a few days. No VIN-level integration to build, so this rises from 4 to 5.

decision_reason: PROVISIONAL: Total 18/25. Demand evidence is weak (score 2), so no GO despite the total.
